challenges.title: An inventory with typed errors
challenges.prompt: Implement apply and parse for a small inventory: commands update an immutable Map, failures are values (Either) and the fold keeps the last good stock when a command fails. This is ordinary Scala 3 code you run on your own machine.
challenges.starter:
enum Cmd:
  case Add(sku: String, qty: Int)
  case Remove(sku: String, qty: Int)

enum InvError:
  case BadQty(n: Int)
  case Unknown(sku: String)
  case Insufficient(sku: String, have: Int, want: Int)

import Cmd.*, InvError.*

type Stock = Map[String, Int]

// TODO: def apply(stock: Stock, cmd: Cmd): Either[InvError, Stock]
//   Add / Remove with qty <= 0 -> Left(BadQty(qty)); Remove of a missing sku -> Left(Unknown(sku));
//   Remove of more than available -> Left(Insufficient(sku, have, want)); otherwise Right(updated stock)
// TODO: def parse(line: String): Option[Cmd]   ("add apple 10" / "remove apple 3"; anything else, including non-numeric qty, is None)

@main def run() =
  val lines = List("add apple 10", "add pear 4", "remove apple 3", "remove kiwi 1", "remove pear 9", "add fig 0", "oops", "add apple 5")
  val (finalStock, errors) = lines.foldLeft((Map.empty: Stock, List.empty[String])) { case ((st, errs), line) =>
    parse(line) match
      case None => (st, errs :+ s"unparsable: $line")
      case Some(c) => apply(st, c) match
        case Right(s2) => (s2, errs)
        case Left(e) => (st, errs :+ e.toString)
  }
  println(finalStock.toList.sortBy(_._1))
  errors.foreach(println)
  println(s"errors=${errors.size}")

challenges.solution:
enum Cmd:
  case Add(sku: String, qty: Int)
  case Remove(sku: String, qty: Int)

enum InvError:
  case BadQty(n: Int)
  case Unknown(sku: String)
  case Insufficient(sku: String, have: Int, want: Int)

import Cmd.*, InvError.*

type Stock = Map[String, Int]

def apply(stock: Stock, cmd: Cmd): Either[InvError, Stock] = cmd match
  case Add(sku, q) if q <= 0 => Left(BadQty(q))
  case Add(sku, q) => Right(stock.updated(sku, stock.getOrElse(sku, 0) + q))
  case Remove(sku, q) if q <= 0 => Left(BadQty(q))
  case Remove(sku, q) =>
    stock.get(sku) match
      case None => Left(Unknown(sku))
      case Some(h) if h < q => Left(Insufficient(sku, h, q))
      case Some(h) => Right(stock.updated(sku, h - q))

def parse(line: String): Option[Cmd] = line.split(" ").toList match
  case "add" :: sku :: q :: Nil => q.toIntOption.map(Add(sku, _))
  case "remove" :: sku :: q :: Nil => q.toIntOption.map(Remove(sku, _))
  case _ => None

@main def run() =
  val lines = List("add apple 10", "add pear 4", "remove apple 3", "remove kiwi 1", "remove pear 9", "add fig 0", "oops", "add apple 5")
  val (finalStock, errors) = lines.foldLeft((Map.empty: Stock, List.empty[String])) { case ((st, errs), line) =>
    parse(line) match
      case None => (st, errs :+ s"unparsable: $line")
      case Some(c) => apply(st, c) match
        case Right(s2) => (s2, errs)
        case Left(e) => (st, errs :+ e.toString)
  }
  println(finalStock.toList.sortBy(_._1))
  errors.foreach(println)
  println(s"errors=${errors.size}")
challenges.explain: Each command returns Either, so errors never throw. The foldLeft threads (stock, errors) through, keeping the previous stock when a command is rejected. Verified by compiling and running with Scala 3.3.1.

challenges.title: Parallel word count with retries
challenges.prompt: Count words in several documents concurrently with Futures, retrying a flaky step with recoverWith, then merge the maps. Futures run on the global execution context; Await is used only at the program edge so the result can be printed.
challenges.explain: Future.traverse starts all documents, recoverWith retries a failing future up to max times and merge sums counts. A document that keeps failing surfaces its exception as a failed future. Verified by compiling and running with Scala 3.3.1.
